question: Does native heightmap collision hold up over the full 100 x 10 m area, and what does it change?
answer: The mission passes: ten tracks, ACQUIRED/HOLD, ESTIMATED_COMPLETE, no scan-motion fault, and the spurious near-horizontal contact normal is gone. The slip audit still fails, but it fails the same way on the triangle-mesh version of this road, and the dominant cause is the audit's duplicate-row test firing on painted markings.

scene.heightmap: 1025x1025 16-bit PNG, 118.4 x 15.4 x 0.005977 m, quantisation 4.6e-8 m

placement_defect_fixed.symptom: the first full-area attempt drove into free fall at x = 59.218 m and faulted with CAMERA_terrain_sampling_failure once the camera's downward rays left the declared height bounds
placement_defect_fixed.cause: gz-physics never applies <heightmap><pos>; the offset reaches DART only through the model pose. The scene contract forbade a nonzero model pose, so the generator had put the offset in <pos> and the collision surface stayed centred on the world origin
placement_defect_fixed.measured_support_before: x in [-59.2, +59.2], which is size.x/2 either side of the origin
placement_defect_fixed.measured_support_after: x = -9.5 and 109 fall through, -9 and 108 are supported, matching the declared [-9.3, 109.1]
placement_defect_fixed.second_consequence: inside the supported band the collision surface was offset 49.9 m in x and about 3 mm high relative to the visual and OptiX surfaces, so the earlier 20 m A/B measured contact on a surface the camera never saw
placement_defect_fixed.why_the_probe_missed_it: the 20 x 2 m A/B only reached x = 20.5 and could not touch a boundary at 59.2 m
fix: tools/create_native_heightmap_scene.py writes the placement as the model pose and leaves <pos> at zero
src/agv_linescan/agv_linescan/shared_scene.py allows that one pose and pins it to the manifest, and requires <pos> to be zero
src/agv_linescan/test/test_shared_scene.py rejects the legacy layout, both-set and neither-set

mission.instance_uptime_note: the instance had been running about 5.5 h, unlike the 3 min of the triangle-mesh comparison run; section 6 showed no RTF decay after the Mesa fix, but the two are not equal-condition

contact.against_triangle_mesh: the mesh baseline reached 89.985 deg of normal tilt and an 18 ms contact gap; here every wheel stays at or below 0.641 deg, which is under the road's own 0.67 deg maximum slope, and no gap exceeds two 1 ms steps
contact.residual_outlier: rl reports a 0.557 mm maximum penetration against 0.065-0.076 mm on the other three. It did not produce a fault and the normal stayed correct, but it is the one contact quantity not yet explained

residual_reading: More samples cross the gate than on the mesh road (1438 against 418) yet none landed during capture and no flight dump was written. The catastrophic class -- a wrong normal driving a 27 kN impulse -- is absent; what remains is the turnaround ill-conditioning that happens with the shutter closed. One clean run does not prove the class is eliminated.

slip_audit.duplicate_rows_are_the_paint: 31 of 704 images here and 32 of 699 on the mesh version of the same road; zero on the unmarked road. A flagged 64-row run in block 78 averages 113.4 grey against 56.9 for ordinary rows, with an adjacent-row difference of 2.0 against 7.0, at x = 92.2 where the manifest places marking polygons. The duplicate test thresholds against a whole-run median, so uniform paint falls below it. This is a detector limitation, not a capture defect, and it will fail every run on a marked road until the test is conditioned on local texture.
slip_audit.slip_attributable_to_the_heightmap: real but small and confined to acceleration: intervals below 0.95 go from 2 to 6 and the 0.1st percentile from 0.9882 to 0.9292. Five of the six sit wholly in the lead-in or run-out (x < 0 or x > 100); one straddles the ROI entry at x in [-0.41, 1.03].

detector_fixed.change: tools/audit_scan_slip.py now divides the adjacent-row difference by the texture measured along the row. A stall keeps each row's own contrast and loses only the difference to its neighbour, so the ratio collapses; paint loses both together, so it does not move. Row pairs with less than a tenth of the run's median texture are reported as untestable instead of passed in silence.
detector_fixed.effect: Flagged images go from 31 to 0 on the heightmap run and 32 to 0 on the mesh version of the same road, while the unmarked baseline stays at 0 and still passes. No row pair was untestable in any of the three.
detector_fixed.statistic_is_stable_across_roads: the difference/texture median is 0.478 on all three runs, against adjacent-row difference medians of 9.13-9.23 and texture medians of 19.06-19.32
detector_fixed.the_remaining_minimum_is_real: the lowest ratio in the heightmap run, 0.1973 against a 0.191 threshold, sits at block 494 row pair 0, x = 104.93 m, where the row texture is a normal 20.3 while the difference is only 4.01. That block is one of the six the encoder-versus-ground test independently flagged, at ratio 0.9395. Two detectors converging on the same place is evidence for both; the thin margin is the real signal approaching the threshold, not a residue of the paint problem.
detector_fixed.still_failing_and_correctly_so: both rough-road runs still fail the audit, now only on encoder-versus-ground slip

not_closed: the slip audit must stop flagging paint before it can gate this road
acceleration slip under heightmap contact is measurably worse than under the mesh and is not explained
one full-area run is not the repeat regression section 6 requires
the scene lives under local_data and is not in Git; the generator command above is the only way back to it
the manifest still declares 48 collision_proxy meshes and shared_scene.validate_proxy still checks them, but world.sdf no longer references any of them: dead geometry that is still validated

corrected_2026_09_16.retracted: An earlier note in this file and in the docs claimed the heightmap removed the crack shallow-depression collision proxies and so changed the COLLISION_PROXY contract. That was a misreading and is withdrawn.
corrected_2026_09_16.what_is_actually_true: COLLISION_PROXY.md describes a proxy that fills shallow depressions away, not one that represents them: 'no longer computes tyre contact inside the 1-2 mm cracks'. The production road's collision has never resolved cracks. All 48 collision meshes in the rough marked v2 asset are pure regular grids -- vertex and triangle counts equal ux*uy and (ux-1)*(uy-1)*2 exactly, with no extra geometry anywhere.
corrected_2026_09_16.so_the_heightmap_changes_nothing_there: it replaces one single-valued non-crack-resolving surface, a 10 cm triangulated heightfield, with another, a 11.6 cm by 1.5 cm heightmap. Same class of representation.
corrected_2026_09_16.found_while_checking: world.sdf contains zero references to terrain_N_collision.obj, yet the manifest still declares them and the validator still walks them
